scenarios.title: Production dies at 87% — encoder 0x80040216

environment.network: 1 Gbps wired to SAN; no VPN
environment.av: Microsoft Defender, real-time on; no folder exclusions for Camtasia
environment.notes: Client delivery contract requires 4K H.264 MP4. Preview plays. Smart Player export fails at the same percent.

scenarios.summary: A 22-minute 4K Camtasia project fails during Share > Local File. Progress reaches 87% then aborts with encoder 0x80040216. Customer already reinstalled Camtasia twice. Client handoff is 4:00 PM today.
scenarios.description:
Hi Support,

We cannot produce our flagship 4K course video. Camtasia gets to 87% and then throws:

  Production failed.
  Encoder error 0x80040216

The timeline has:
- 4K screen recording (MP4)
- 3 picture-in-picture camera shots
- 14 annotations + 2 behaviors
- Audiate-cleaned voiceover on a separate track

Preview plays fine. Smart Player export also fails at the same point. MP4 (H.264) is the required delivery format.

This is blocking a paid client handoff today. Please treat as urgent.

Priya

[2026-08-24 08:57:11] Profile: MP4 4K (3840x2160) 30fps AAC 48kHz

diagnosticSteps.prompt: What is the strongest first diagnostic move?

options.label: Parse the production log and identify encoder, HWAccel, and the failure frame.
options.feedback: Correct. The log already names NVENC, a submit timeout, and “device removed.” That frames this as a hardware-encoder failure, not a license or corrupt-install issue.

options.label: Have the customer reinstall Camtasia a third time and repair Visual C++ runtimes.
options.feedback: Weak. Preview works and the log never mentions missing runtimes. Reinstall theater burns the remaining deadline.

options.label: Ask whether the project and media live on a network share, then copy locally as a test.
options.feedback: Reasonable hygiene — NAS stutter can worsen encoder timeouts — but the log already pinpoints NVENC device-removed. Treat storage as a secondary check.

options.label: Increase Camtasia’s RAM allotment in Preferences and retry the same 4K HW encode.
options.feedback: Camtasia does not expose a RAM “allotment” that would fix NVENC 0x80040216. This is a GPU encoder path problem.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: NVENC timed out at 87%. Which mitigation should you try first while preserving 4K H.264 delivery?

options.label: Disable hardware encoding (Edit > Preferences > Advanced) and produce with the software H.264 encoder.
options.feedback: Best same-day workaround. Software encode is slower but typically bypasses NVENC device-removed failures so the client file can still ship.

options.label: Tell them the RTX 4070 is unsupported and they must replace the GPU before producing.
options.feedback: Incorrect. RTX 4070 is fully supported. This is a driver/encoder-path issue, not a hardware-eligibility issue.

options.label: Have them install the latest NVIDIA Studio driver, then retry hardware encoding.
options.feedback: Good medium-term fix — Game Ready 551.23 is a known noisy combo with NVENC under long 4K sessions — but it is slower than switching to software encode for a 4:00 PM deadline.

options.label: Force 1080p production so they can “just send something.”
options.feedback: That changes the contracted deliverable. Use it only if software 4K encode is impossible, and get the customer’s buy-in first.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: How should this ticket be closed out for a P1 client deadline?

options.label: Ship the software-encode workaround, collect GPU-Z + the produce log, and file a hardware-encoder defect with Engineering if software succeeds.
options.feedback: This is the escalation pattern: unblock the customer, preserve evidence, then loop Engineering with a reproducible encoder signature.

options.label: Close as “customer hardware problem” once you mention drivers.
options.feedback: Do not close a reproducing encoder abort as “customer hardware” without a successful workaround and a paper trail.

options.label: Escalate to Engineering immediately with no workaround and no log excerpts.
options.feedback: Engineering will bounce this. Always include encoder name, driver version, failure percent, and the workaround result.

options.label: Recommend producing a proxy timeline at 1/4 resolution as the only path forward.
options.feedback: Useful if software 4K is also failing, but it should not be the first closeout plan on a 4K H.264 contract.

emailCriteria.tone: Urgent but calm. Acknowledge the 4:00 PM client deadline in the first two sentences, then give a same-day workaround before any driver discussion.
requiredElements: Empathy for the paid client handoff / deadline
Cite NVENC / encoder 0x80040216 from the produce log
Exact path: Edit > Preferences > Advanced to disable hardware encoding
Software H.264 encode as the same-day path; Studio driver as follow-up
Ask them to confirm a successful produce and attach the new log if it still fails
modelReplyHints: Acknowledge the client deadline.
Cite the NVENC timeout in the production log.
Give the exact path to disable hardware encoding.
Offer a driver update as the follow-up, not the blocker.

scenarios.title: Chrome window records as a black rectangle

environment.disk: Local 1 TB NVMe; project on Desktop (not OneDrive)
environment.display: Laptop 1920x1200 @ 150% + HDMI 1080p @ 100% when docked (issue happens undocked too)
environment.av: CrowdStrike Falcon (IT-managed); cannot install extra utilities
environment.notes: Chrome 127 and Edge both black; Firefox window capture is fine. Desktop/full-screen capture is fine.

scenarios.summary: Full-screen recordings of the desktop look normal, but a region or window capture of Google Chrome (Canvas LMS + slides) is a black box with a visible cursor. Audio is fine. Started after a Chrome update. School laptop — no random installs.
scenarios.description:
Hello,

I record software demos of our Canvas LMS in Chrome. This week every Camtasia recording of the Chrome window is just black. I can see my mouse, and you can hear me, but the browser contents are gone.

I tried:
- New Camtasia project
- Different Chrome profile
- Window capture and region capture (both black)
- Full screen / full desktop (this looks fine, but I do not want my email popups)

Edge does the same thing. Firefox records correctly. I am on a school laptop and cannot install random utilities without IT.

Thanks,
Elena

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Desktop capture works, Chrome/Edge window capture is black, Firefox is fine. What does that tell you?

options.label: This is almost certainly GPU hardware acceleration / video overlay in Chromium, not a corrupt Camtasia install.
options.feedback: Right pattern. WGC cannot see D3D hardware overlays. Chromium after a GPU update is the classic black-window capture case.

options.label: Reinstall Camtasia 2023 and repair the recorder codec pack.
options.feedback: Desktop capture already works, so the recorder is healthy. Reinstall will not change Chrome’s overlay behavior.

options.label: Mismatch the project sample rate to 44.1 kHz because audio can desync black frames.
options.feedback: Audio is explicitly fine. Sample rate drift is a different class of ticket, not a black rectangle.

options.label: Check Windows Privacy > Screen recording permissions for Camtasia.
options.feedback: Worth a 10-second glance on 24H2, but a permission failure would typically block desktop capture too — which works here.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Customer cannot install extra tools. Which fix should you lead with?

options.label: Disable hardware acceleration in Chrome/Edge (Settings > System) and set Windows Graphics to High performance for chrome.exe if needed.
options.feedback: The standard, IT-friendly fix. Forces Chromium to compose in a capturable path without new software.

options.label: Tell them Camtasia cannot record browsers and they must switch to OBS.
options.feedback: Incorrect and abandons the product. Window capture of browsers is supported once overlays are disabled.

options.label: Insist they only ever record full desktop and crop in the editor.
options.feedback: Valid workaround (they already know desktop works) but it reintroduces notification leak risk. Offer it as Plan B.

options.label: DDU the AMD driver and install an old recommended driver before recording again.
options.feedback: Too heavy for a school laptop, and Firefox already captures on the same GPU. Treat driver work as last resort.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: How do you make sure this does not bounce back next Chrome update?

options.label: Have them test a 15-second window capture, then mention chrome://flags overlays and Windows Game Bar conflict as fallbacks.
options.feedback: Closes the loop with a verification recording and names the two most common leftover overlay sources.

options.label: Close the ticket as user error for recording the wrong window.
options.feedback: The log names Chrome_WidgetWin_1 and hardware overlays. This is not operator error.

options.label: Tell them the issue is fixed only in Camtasia 2024 and they must purchase an upgrade.
options.feedback: Do not upsell a Chromium overlay problem. 2023 can record the window once acceleration is off.

options.label: Document Firefox as the only supported browser for LMS recordings.
options.feedback: A workable departmental policy, but Chrome is their LMS standard — give them a Chrome path first.

emailCriteria.tone: Friendly faculty support. Do not ask a locked-down school laptop to install extra recorders.
requiredElements: Acknowledge that desktop capture working isolates the issue to Chromium overlays
Chrome/Edge: Settings > System > disable hardware acceleration
Ask for a short test window capture
Full-desktop + crop only as backup (notification leak risk)
modelReplyHints: Acknowledge that desktop capture working isolates this to Chromium overlays.
Give the Chrome/Edge hardware acceleration path.
Ask for a short test recording.
Offer full-desktop + crop only as a backup.

scenarios.title: Voiceover drifts ~1.5s by the 12-minute mark

environment.disk: Internal NVMe (project); VO WAV copied from a Zoom H6 SD card
environment.notes: Timeline sample rate 48 kHz. Imported VO is 44.1 kHz 24-bit WAV. Screen recording AAC is 48 kHz. Audiate was not used on this file.

scenarios.summary: A 18-minute software tutorial looks in sync at 0:00, but the voiceover is almost a second and a half late by 12:00. Customer “stretched” the clip, which made it worse. Preview and produced MP4 both drift.
scenarios.description:
Hi,

I imported a Zoom H6 voiceover WAV under a Camtasia screen recording. At the start, picture and voice match. By the middle of the video the VO is late, and by the end it is obviously off. I tried Clip Speed and stretching the audio to the end marker — now it is worse in the first half too.

Camtasia project is 1920x1080 30fps. I did not change any audio preferences. The WAV plays fine in VLC and is the correct length on paper (18:04).

Please tell me if I need to re-record. Talent is not available until next week.

Jonah
scenarios.crashLog:
[Project] frameRate=30.000  audioSampleRate=48000  channels=2
[Media] ARoll_Screen.trec  audio=AAC 48000 Hz  16-bit  duration=1084.02s
[Media] VO_H6_Master.wav  pcm_s24le  44100 Hz  2ch  duration=1084.18s
[Timeline] audio.resample=implicit  44100 → 48000 (low-quality)
[Produce] AAC 48 kHz  — drift vs video clock ~ +1480ms at t=720s
[Note] no time-stretch markers except user Clip Speed 99.2% on VO track
[Device] H6 recorded at 44.1 kHz (file header confirmed)

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Preview and produce both drift, and the VO file is 44.1 kHz in a 48 kHz project. First move?

options.label: Treat this as a sample-rate conversion / clock-drift issue: inspect source Hz vs project Hz before touching clip speed.
options.feedback: Correct. 44.1 into 48 with a cheap implicit resample is a classic accumulating drift. Clip Speed is the wrong tool.

options.label: Tell them the H6 recording is corrupt and they must re-record talent.
options.feedback: The WAV duration matches and VLC plays it. Do not burn a talent session until you convert sample rate cleanly.

options.label: Disable hardware encoding because NVENC is known to desync audio.
options.feedback: NVENC can cause produce failures, not a linear 1.5s VO drift that also appears in preview.

options.label: Unlink audio from the .trec and delete the VO, then use Camtasia’s narration recorder only.
options.feedback: A last-resort workflow change. The H6 file is salvageable with a proper resample.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: How should they repair the media without a re-record?

options.label: Convert the WAV to 48 kHz (Audiate, Adobe Audition, or ffmpeg) and replace the timeline clip with the 48 kHz file; reset Clip Speed to 100%.
options.feedback: Matches the project clock. Replacing the clip avoids the implicit low-quality resample Camtasia already logged.

options.label: Change the entire Camtasia project sample rate to 44.1 kHz and re-produce.
options.feedback: Can work but the screen recording is already 48 kHz AAC; you would resample the larger A-roll instead of one VO file.

options.label: Keep Clip Speed and add more keyframes until it “sounds close.”
options.feedback: Manual speed ramps will not track a linear resample error and will damage consonants.

options.label: Switch the project from 30fps to 29.97 to absorb the drift.
options.feedback: Frame rate is not the clock that is slipping. This will not fix 44.1 vs 48.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: What should the reply teach so this does not recur?

options.label: Document an ingest rule: match VO sample rate to the Camtasia project (48 kHz) before import; avoid Clip Speed for sync.
options.feedback: Prevents the next H6 dump from hitting the same implicit resample.

options.label: Tell them Zoom H6 is unsupported with Camtasia.
options.feedback: H6 WAVs are supported. The bug is sample-rate hygiene, not the recorder brand.

options.label: Require every VO to be run through Audiate even if they do not want transcription.
options.feedback: Audiate can resample, but it is not mandatory if they convert with any 48 kHz export.

options.label: Close as expected behavior and offer no conversion steps.
options.feedback: Customers need a concrete conversion path, not a shrug.

emailCriteria.tone: Practical editor-to-editor. Reassure that talent does not need to re-record if they convert the WAV.
requiredElements: Name the 44.1 kHz VO vs 48 kHz project mismatch
Tell them to reset Clip Speed to 100%
Give a conversion path to 48 kHz and replace the clip
Ingest rule for next time
modelReplyHints: Reassure that the H6 file is salvageable.
Explain 44.1 vs 48 kHz as the cause of accumulating drift.
Give numbered steps: convert, replace clip, reset speed, spot-check 12:00.
Warn that Clip Speed is the wrong fix.

scenarios.title: 4K timeline stutters in preview; playhead skips

environment.disk: 512 GB SSD with 28 GB free; project in ~/Movies/Camtasia
environment.network: Wi-Fi 6E; iCloud Drive Desktop & Documents ON
environment.notes: Source is 4K 60fps iPhone + 4K screen recording. Preview drops to ~8 fps with three tracks and Behaviors. Produce to 1080p completes, but they cannot edit.

scenarios.summary: Editing a 4K multi-track project on an M1 Pro is nearly unusable: preview stutters, the playhead skips, and ripple edits take several seconds. Export to 1080p works. Customer thinks Camtasia is “broken on Apple silicon.”
scenarios.description:
Hello TechSmith,

Camtasia on my M1 Pro is unusable for this product launch video. The timeline has:
- 4K 60fps iPhone b-roll
- 4K screen recording of our app
- music + VO

Playback in the canvas is choppy (I counted the playhead jumping). Adding a callout hangs the UI for 4–5 seconds. I already toggled Power Save off.

Exporting 1080p last night worked, so I do not think the media is corrupt. I need to actually edit today.

Is Camtasia not optimized for Apple silicon? Should I move back to my old Intel iMac?

Mei

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Produce works but preview is 8 fps and disk free space is 28 GB with iCloud eviction. Where do you start?

options.label: Turn on editing proxies / lower canvas quality and free local disk so iCloud-evicted media is fully local.
options.feedback: This is a playback-performance ticket, not an Apple-silicon defect. Proxies plus local media are the first two levers.

options.label: Confirm that Camtasia is broken on M1 and recommend they buy an Intel Mac.
options.feedback: Camtasia is Apple-silicon native. Produce succeeding already disproves “broken on M1.”

options.label: Reinstall Camtasia x86 under Rosetta to “improve stability.”
options.feedback: Rosetta would likely make Metal playback worse. Do not recommend it.

options.label: Tell them 16 GB is unsupported and they must buy a 64 GB Mac before editing.
options.feedback: 16 GB is tight for 4K60 HEVC, but proxies are the supported path before hardware upsell.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Which concrete editor settings should you send?

options.label: View > Project Settings: generate proxy files; set preview quality to 1/4; keep produce target at 1080p.
options.feedback: Decouples edit playback from 4K60 HEVC decode. Matches how Camtasia is meant to be used on 16 GB machines.

options.label: Have them transcode every clip to animation 4K ProRes in Finder before importing, no proxies.
options.feedback: Works but is slow and disk-hungry on a 28 GB-free volume. Proxies are lighter.

options.label: Force OpenGL renderer in a hidden plist.
options.feedback: Unsupported and obsolete on Sonoma. Do not send plist hacks on Tier 2.

options.label: Tell them Camtasia only supports one 4K track and they must delete the iPhone footage.
options.feedback: False product limitation. Multi-track 4K is supported with proxies.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Disk is nearly full and iCloud evicted two files. How do you close?

options.label: Move the project off iCloud Desktop, download evicted originals, keep 50+ GB free, then generate proxies.
options.feedback: Evicted placeholders plus 4K HEVC is a stutter factory. Local full-resolution media is required before blaming the app.

options.label: Ignore iCloud; stutter is only a GPU issue.
options.feedback: The log explicitly shows iCloud.evicted=true for two files.

options.label: Close with a sales quote for Camtasia 2025.
options.feedback: This is configuration, not a version entitlement issue.

options.label: Suggest an external SSD for media as an optional capacity fix after proxies.
options.feedback: Good capacity advice, but it is secondary to proxies + downloading evicted files today.

emailCriteria.tone: Reassure that M1 is supported. Stay out of “buy a new Mac” unless they still stutter after proxies and local media.
requiredElements: Camtasia is Apple-silicon native; produce success proves the app runs
Enable proxy / 1/4 preview quality
Download iCloud-evicted files and keep more free disk
Keep final produce at 1080p if that is the delivery
modelReplyHints: Reject the “broken on Apple silicon” frame using the successful 1080p produce.
Give proxy + preview-quality steps.
Call out iCloud eviction and free disk.
Invite them back if playback is still <15 fps after proxies.

scenarios.title: Project opens with 11 offline media clips after OneDrive sync

environment.disk: OneDrive Known Folder Move: Desktop+Documents; Files On-Demand = ON
environment.network: Zscaler ZIA; OneDrive sync “online-only” for files >100 MB
environment.notes: Grant-funded gala video due tonight. .tscproj opens but most .trec/.mp4 show Media Offline. Recycle Bin empty. Second PC at home shows the same OneDrive folder with placeholders.

scenarios.summary: After IT enabled OneDrive Files On-Demand, a 40-minute gala project opens with a cascade of Media Offline. Customer cannot find the original .trec files. They already ran Repair Project. Deadline is tonight’s donor event.
scenarios.description:
We are in trouble.

Our gala highlight reel (Camtasia project on the Desktop) opened this morning with gray Media Offline blocks. I can see file names like Gala_CamA.trec but Windows says “cloud outline” icons. Double-clicking in Explorer downloads a 1 KB pointer, not the recording.

IT turned on OneDrive Files On-Demand Friday. I did not move anything. Repair Project did nothing. Copying the .tscproj to D: still shows offline media.

Donors see this video at 7:00 PM. I need the actual recordings back or a recovery path.

Diego

options.feedback: Right. Repair Project cannot relink files the cloud never fully stored or will not download.

options.label: Reinstall Camtasia 2023 to rebuild the media index.

options.feedback: Splits recovery (cache) from prevention (DLP + pinning). This is the only honest P1 path.

options.label: Tell them to wait 24 hours for OneDrive to “finish thinking.”
options.feedback: DLP denied hydration. Waiting will not change a block rule before the gala.

options.label: Have them play a produced MP4 from last week if one exists, then re-record the gala from the audience.

options.label: Send a PhotoRec tutorial to carve .trec off the SSD themselves.
options.feedback: Too expert and too slow for a 7 PM event unless IT forensics is already in the room.

options.label: Give IT a short brief: exclude TechSmith recordings from online-only/DLP, pin the project folder, and keep a local non-OneDrive working copy for Camtasia.
options.feedback: Fixes the org issue, not just tonight’s file. Camtasia projects do not belong on Files On-Demand.

options.label: Tell the customer their IT department is incompetent and to disable OneDrive entirely.
options.feedback: Unprofessional and may violate their security policy. Partner with IT.

options.label: Document “never use OneDrive” with no pinning/DLP guidance.
options.feedback: Directionally true for active .trec files, but enterprises need a pinned-folder pattern, not a ban with no alternative.

options.label: File as a Camtasia bug because it should hydrate OneDrive placeholders automatically.
options.feedback: Editor cannot override Zscaler DLP. Do not dump this on Engineering as a hydrate feature request on a P1 night.

emailCriteria.tone: Crisis-calm. Do not promise the files definitely exist in the cloud. Partner with IT; do not dunk on them.
requiredElements: Explain Files On-Demand placeholders vs missing media
Mention Zscaler DLP hydration deny from the log
Recovery: MediaCache + IT allow/pin .trec
Standing guidance: Camtasia working copies local or Always keep on this device
modelReplyHints: Name OneDrive placeholders and the DLP deny, not a corrupt project.
Give IT-facing pin/exclude steps.
Hunt MediaCache for any fragments.
Set a local working-copy standard after the event.

scenarios.title: Snagit activation succeeds, then prompts again on launch

environment.notes: Volume key valid in TechSmith account. 180 seats. Labs are air-gapped. Started after Friday PAC change.

scenarios.summary: Enterprise seats activate in the wizard (“You’re all set”) then return to activation on the next cold start. IT confirmed the key. Proxy/PAC and SSL inspection changed Friday. Labs need an offline path.
scenarios.description:
Support,

We deployed Snagit 2024 with our volume key via Intune. Users complete activation (sometimes with our software key, sometimes online). The UI says success. Next cold start: activation screen again.

What we already tried:
- Re-entered the key
- Ran Snagit as admin
- Disabled the Windows firewall profile (no change)
- Recreated one user profile (still loops)

Our network team switched PAC files Friday. Outbound SSL inspection is on. I can whitelist if you give me exact destinations.

Need a stable activation path for 180 seats. Offline/locked-down lab machines are in scope too.

Marcus Hale — Desktop Engineering

[Activation]
key.status=accepted
license.type=enterprise
server.response=200 OK (first handshake)
token.write=FAILED  path=%PROGRAMDATA%\TechSmith\Snagit\License
token.error=Access denied (0x80070005)
fallback.write=FAILED  HKLM\SOFTWARE\TechSmith\Snagit\24\License

diagnosticSteps.prompt: The UI reports success but the next launch is unlicensed. Where do you look first?

options.label: Inspect whether Snagit can persist a license token under ProgramData / HKLM after “success.”
options.feedback: Correct. This is a persist-after-activate failure (0x80070005), not a bad key. The loop is almost always ACL, SYSTEM context, or SSL inspection.

options.label: Issue a new software key and have every user activate again.
options.feedback: The current key already validates. Burning seats will not fix a token write or proxy-trust problem.

options.label: Reset Snagit preferences by deleting %AppData%\TechSmith\Snagit.
options.feedback: Harmless but incomplete. Preferences are per-user; this machine-wide MSI needs a writable machine license location.

options.label: Delete the entire HKLM\SOFTWARE\TechSmith tree and reboot.
options.feedback: Too blunt. You can destroy deployment settings and still leave the ACL / SSL-inspection root cause in place.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Logs show SSL inspection on licensing hosts and SYSTEM not trusting the interceptor cert. What next?

options.label: Whitelist activation.techsmith.com and licensing.techsmith.com (no SSL intercept) and deploy the inspection root to Local Machine Trusted Root.
options.feedback: This is the enterprise fix: either bypass intercept on licensing endpoints or trust the inspector at machine scope so SYSTEM activation can succeed.

options.label: Have users turn off Windows Defender and retry activation.
options.feedback: Defender is not in the log. Do not ask a bank to disable AV as a licensing workaround.

options.label: Switch the install to per-user and let each employee activate in their own context.
options.feedback: Can work around SYSTEM ACL issues, but it fights a machine-wide Intune MSI and still leaves SSL inspection broken for some users.

options.label: Ignore the proxy change; activation returned 200 so the network is fine.
options.feedback: A 200 on the first handshake does not mean the token write succeeded, and intercept without a machine-trusted cert breaks later launches.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: IT also has locked-down lab PCs. How do you complete the reply?

options.label: Provide offline activation for labs, plus an Intune script to grant SYSTEM write access on the TechSmith license folder for the online fleet.
options.feedback: Covers both topologies: air-gapped labs get offline activation; managed desktops get a writable license store and trusted licensing hosts.

Leila

options.feedback: They already did. The blit happens after that flag.

The video includes EHR screens. We believe one chapter shows patient names. We need:
1) how to kill public access immediately
2) why Unlisted was searchable
3) whether folder permissions overrode the video
4) what to tell Legal about cache/CDN

Do not ask us to “edit the video later” as the only step.

Imani Brooks, Privacy

[Folder] /Meridian/L&D/Contractors  acl=anyone-in-org

options.label: Google hacked Screencast and they should sue Google first.

options.label: Unlisted is equivalent to HIPAA-safe and no further action is required.

options.label: Wipe the entire Screencast business account immediately.

options.label: Only blur names in Camtasia and re-upload, leaving the old URL up.
options.feedback: Old URL stays public. They already said editing later is not enough.

options.label: Changing the folder to Private is enough; ignore Google cache and CDN TTL.

options.label: Have Marketing tweet that the link is invalid.

options.label: Offer a higher SKU as the fix for the exposure.

options.label: Disable Chrome hardware acceleration.

options.label: Document that each teacher should click Reset Privacy in Terminal.

options.label: Say this is fixed only if they buy Camtasia 2025 today.
options.feedback: The log is a signature pin, not a SKU entitlement.

emailCriteria.tone: Calm K-12. Address both Grace (what to try) and IT (PPPC). Do not ask a student-device Mac to disable SIP.

Jamf PPPC code-requirement mismatch, not a broken recorder
IT must update the Screen Recording payload for the current bundle
Quit Camtasia fully and recapture after the profile lands

Ben Ortiz

options.feedback: False. Offline just froze the trial cache.

emailCriteria.tone: License-accurate and unblocking. Do not paste keys. Do not promise a free site license. Offer a today path for the VO.

Sign Audiate in with the org Okta identity, not Gmail trial
Do not paste the Camtasia software key into Audiate
CSAM/order alignment if they were sold a bundle
modelReplyHints: Separate Camtasia activation from Audiate’s trial identity.
Get Audiate on the org account.
Do not use the Camtasia key in Audiate.

scenarios.title: Screencast.com view counts stay at zero for an assigned course

environment.app: Screencast.com Library + Camtasia Share to Screencast
environment.network: School filter; privacy=Anyone with the link; videos played inside a Google Sites embed
environment.notes: Teacher dashboard Views = 0 after 90 staff watched in a PD session. Individual play progress in the player looked normal. Embed is an old iframe to a collection page, not the player URL. Do Not Track / cookie banner dismissed on some devices.

scenarios.summary: A PD video on Screencast.com was watched by a full staff meeting. Analytics still show 0 views. Customer needs attendance evidence for the grant.
scenarios.description:
Hi,

We played our Screencast PD video for 90 teachers this morning (Google Sites page on the projector and on their laptops). Screencast Analytics still says 0 views and 0 unique viewers.

The video definitely played. Privacy is Anyone with the link.

I need numbers for a grant report Friday.

Maya
scenarios.crashLog:
[Asset] privacy=anyone-with-link  analytics=on
[Embed] google-sites iframe src=https://www.screencast.com/users/lakeside/folders/PD2026
[Embed] type=folder listing  not player  (plays via nested player with sandbox)
[Hits] pageview.folder=90  media.play.beacon=0  (sandbox allow-scripts missing; beacon blocked)
[Player] direct URL  beacons OK in Control Room test
[Filter] Lightspeed allows screencast.com GET  blocks some POST /telemetry
[Note] Unique viewers require signed-in Library users; anonymous plays still increment Views if beacons fire

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Folder-page iframe + sandbox + possible POST telemetry block. Why 0 views?

options.label: Analytics beacons never fired from the Google Sites folder embed (sandbox/telemetry), not “Screencast lost the video.”
options.feedback: Folder listing hits ≠ media play beacons. Direct player URL still counts.

options.label: The file is corrupt so plays do not count.
options.feedback: They watched it. Media is fine.

options.label: Views only count if every teacher has a TechSmith account.
options.feedback: Unique viewers may require identity; raw Views should still increment when beacons fire. Do not force 90 new accounts as the first fix.

options.label: Analytics are 24 hours delayed always.
options.feedback: There can be ingest delay, but 90 plays with 0 beacons is the embed, not a daily batch.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Grant report Friday. How do they get honest numbers going forward, and what can we say about this morning?

options.label: Switch the Sites embed to the video player share/oEmbed (not the folder URL), ask filter to allow Screencast telemetry POSTs, and explain this morning’s 90 plays likely will not backfill.
options.feedback: Fixes the next PD and is honest that beacons cannot be invented retroactively.

options.label: Offer to type 90 views into analytics for the grant.
options.feedback: We do not fabricate analytics.

options.label: Move the video to YouTube to get numbers.
options.feedback: They asked to fix Screencast analytics.

options.label: Require TechSmith logins for all staff before any PD.
options.feedback: Heavy for K-12. Use only if they need per-person unique viewers.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: What should the grant language look like?

options.label: State that attendance was observed in the session; Screencast view beacons were blocked by the embed/filter so the dashboard is not the system of record for this meeting; next session will use the player embed.
options.feedback: Protects the customer from submitting a 0 that looks like nobody watched.

options.label: Tell the grantor that 0 views means nobody watched.
options.feedback: We know they watched. Do not create a compliance incident.

options.label: Delete and re-upload to reset counters.
options.feedback: Will not backfill and breaks the link.

options.label: Ask them to enable Flash for analytics.
options.feedback: Not a thing in 2026.

emailCriteria.tone: K-12 practical and honest about what analytics can and cannot backfill. Do not fabricate 90 views.
requiredElements: Folder iframe did not fire play beacons
Use the video player share/embed, not the folder URL
This morning’s 90 plays likely will not appear later
Do not invent analytics for the grant
modelReplyHints: Separate “we watched it” from “beacons reached Screencast.”
Change to the player embed.
Mention filter POST blocking if IT is in the thread.
Be honest that historical 0s will not backfill.

scenarios.title: Replace video on Screencast keeps old comments on the wrong timeline

environment.notes: Replaced a 16-minute course with an 11:40 recut (Audiate cleanup). Same share URL (good). Comments and canvas drawings from reviewers still sit at the old timestamps. Table of contents chapters are the old length. Stakeholders think the new cut is “wrong.”

scenarios.summary: Camtasia Share > Replace kept the Screencast URL, but comments, drawings, and chapters still follow the 16-minute version. New file is 11:40. Stakeholder review is this afternoon.
scenarios.description:
Hi Support,

I used Replace on our Screencast video so the Slack link would stay the same. The new cut is 11:40. The page still shows comments at 14:02 (that time does not exist) and the chapter list is the old one.

People are commenting “the VO is still long” because they are reading old notes.

I need the same URL. I do not want to lose the conversation if we can migrate it. Afternoon review is at 3:00.

Jordan
scenarios.crashLog:
[Replace] asset.id=vid_22ab  url=unchanged  duration.old=962s  duration.new=700s
[Media] blob=swapped  transcode=complete
[Comments] stored as abs_ms on asset.id  NOT remapped  (14:02 → 842000ms still attached)
[TOC] chapters[]  copied from previous  end>new.duration
[Drawings] canvas.overlay  keyed by old media hash  fallback=show anyway
[Share] replaceExisting=true  from Camtasia 2024.1
[Note] no UI prompt “reset comments/chapters” during replace

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Media blob replaced; comment timestamps and TOC were not remapped. Product behavior?

options.label: Replace updates the file and keeps the URL; it does not remap comments/chapters to a shorter timeline. This is expected-but-sharp, not a failed upload.
options.feedback: Explains the 14:02 ghosts without blaming the new VO.

options.label: Replace failed silently; they are still on the old MP4.
options.feedback: Duration in the log is 700s. Media did swap.

options.label: Slack cached the 16-minute file; ignore Screencast.
options.feedback: Comments live on the Screencast asset, not in Slack.

options.label: Audiate Send is what left the comments behind.
options.feedback: This is Screencast Replace semantics.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Same URL required, review at 3:00. What do you do with comments/TOC?

options.label: Keep the URL; clear or export comments; rebuild chapters for 11:40; post a pinned note that timestamps before replace are invalid; optional CSV export if they need the old thread for archive.
options.feedback: Preserves the link and stops false review comments this afternoon.

options.label: Force a brand-new Screencast URL and update Slack only.
options.feedback: They asked to keep the URL. Only if reset is impossible.

options.label: Leave 14:02 comments so “history is preserved” with no warning.
options.feedback: That is what is confusing stakeholders now.

options.label: Time-stretch the 11:40 file back to 16 minutes to match comments.
options.feedback: Destroys the Audiate work.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Should Engineering change Replace?

options.label: File a UX defect: Replace on duration change should prompt to remap/clear comments and TOC; meanwhile document it for authors.
options.feedback: Correct escalation plus a same-day authoring rule.

options.label: Silently delete all comments on every replace forever, no prompt.
options.feedback: Too aggressive as a default. Prompting is the product fix.

options.label: Close as user error for using Replace.
options.feedback: Replace is the advertised way to keep a URL.

options.label: Tell the company to turn off Screencast comments globally.
options.feedback: They want the review workflow.

emailCriteria.tone: Author-friendly before a 3:00 review. Protect the share URL. Be explicit that Replace does not remap timestamps.
requiredElements: Replace kept the URL and swapped media; comments/chapters did not remap
Clear or archive old timestamps; rebuild TOC for 11:40
Pin a note that pre-replace comments are invalid
Do not stretch the new cut to match old notes
modelReplyHints: Affirm the URL is supposed to stay the same.
Explain comments are absolute timestamps.
Give a pre-review cleanup checklist.
Offer to file the missing Replace prompt.

scenarios.title: Password-protected Screencast video still plays in an old embed

environment.app: Screencast.com Business + password on asset + Camtasia Share embed snippet from 2023
environment.network: Okta SSO for staff; contractors use password link
environment.notes: After the unlisted incident, they set a password on the video. The Screencast watch page prompts. An old WordPress embed (iframe with a media ID and a legacy embed token) still plays without a password. Legal wants it confirmed in writing. CDN TTL 24h.

scenarios.summary: A password was added to a PHI-adjacent training video. The Screencast.com page asks for it. An old website embed still streams the file without a prompt. Privacy wants containment this afternoon.
scenarios.description:
This is a follow-up to our privacy ticket.

We set a password on the video. Opening the Screencast link now asks for it. Our public WordPress page (embed from 2023) still plays the full video with no password.

I need:
1) how to kill the embed token immediately
2) whether password applies to all playback surfaces
3) written language for Legal

Do not tell us to “just unpublish WordPress” as the only control — we may not own that CMS today.

Imani Brooks, Privacy
scenarios.crashLog:
[Asset] vid_9f2c  privacy=password  password.set=2026-08-28T13:10Z
[WatchPage] gate=password  OK
[Embed] wordpress iframe  src=https://www.screencast.com/embed/LEGACYTOKEN_2019
[Auth] embed.token.type=legacy-media  not bound to password flag (pre-2021 tokens)
[CDN] /media/vid_9f2c  cookie=embed_legacy  TTL=24h  still 200
[SSO] not invoked on embed path
[Audit] plays.from=wordpress.meridian.example  n=4 after password set

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Password gates the watch page; a pre-2021 embed token still authorizes CDN. Read it as?

options.label: Password is not retroactive to legacy embed tokens. Treat the WordPress iframe as a live unauthenticated playback path.
options.feedback: Privacy officers need surface-by-surface truth, not “we set a password.”

options.label: WordPress stole the password; call Microsoft.
options.feedback: The log is a TechSmith legacy embed token, not a CMS vendor breach.

options.label: If the watch page prompts, the video is fully protected everywhere.
options.feedback: Disproven by the embed 200s after the flag was set.

options.label: Only wait 24 hours for CDN; no other action.
options.feedback: TTL matters, but the token must be revoked or the asset unpublished now.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: They may not control WordPress today. Immediate TechSmith-side kill?

options.label: Revoke/regenerate embed tokens, set the asset to Private/SSO, rotate the share URL, purge CDN, then confirm the legacy iframe 401/404; WordPress cleanup is follow-up.
options.feedback: Contains from the source even if CMS access is delayed.

options.label: Refuse to act until they delete the iframe themselves.
options.feedback: They said they may not own the CMS today. We can still kill the token.

options.label: Set a longer password and assume embeds pick it up.
options.feedback: Legacy tokens are not bound to the password flag.

options.label: Rename the video title so the embed “loses” it.
options.feedback: The media ID still plays.

diagnosticSteps.prompt: Written language for Legal?

options.label: Write: password applies to the Screencast watch page; legacy embed tokens are a separate authz path; N plays after the password; containment = revoke token + private/SSO + purge; we do not declare a HIPAA breach.
options.feedback: Facts, counts, and controls. No legal conclusion.

options.label: Declare a HIPAA breach in the support email.
options.feedback: Legal owns that determination.

options.label: Hide the 4 post-password plays to reduce alarm.
options.feedback: They need the audit number.

options.label: Say only a higher SKU can password-protect embeds.
options.feedback: Do not upsell a privacy event. Fix tokens on this plan.

emailCriteria.tone: Incident-response factual. No humor. Password ≠ all surfaces. Do not declare HIPAA. Give revoke steps they can do in the Screencast UI/account.
requiredElements: Legacy embed token bypasses the watch-page password
Revoke embed / set Private / rotate URL / purge CDN now
WordPress is follow-up, not the only control
Do not declare a HIPAA breach; include post-password play count
modelReplyHints: Split watch-page gate vs legacy embed token.
Lead with revoke/private/purge.
Quote post-password play count.
Leave breach determination to Legal.
